The text editor (texteditor.html) edits text files and source code: several files in tabs, syntax highlighting for more than 40 languages (including SAS, with code completion), search and replace, multiple cursors, and control over encoding and line endings.

Opening and creating files

  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens one or more files; you can also drag files onto the window.
  • New (Alt+N) creates an empty document.
  • Recent (Chrome/Edge on the desktop) reopens recently used files.

Every file opens in its own tab. A dot (●) on a tab shows unsaved changes. Close a tab with × or Alt+W; if it has unsaved changes, the editor asks first. With the keyboard, move to a tab with Tab and press Enter to show it or Delete to close it.

Saving

  • Save (Ctrl+S) writes the file. In Chrome/Edge on the desktop the opened file is changed directly; in Firefox and on Android the file is downloaded – replace the original file with it.
  • Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) saves under a new name. New documents are always saved with "Save as".

Editing

Function Keys
Find / replace (also with regular expressions) Ctrl+F, or 🔍
Go to line Ctrl+G, or ↧
Add a cursor Ctrl+click
Column of cursors (rectangular selection) Alt+drag with the mouse
Select the next occurrence of the word Ctrl+D
Undo / redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z
Indent: the selected lines, or up to the next indentation stop at the cursor / unindent Tab / Shift+Tab
Insert a tab character (whatever the indentation setting) Ctrl+Alt+I
Leave the editor with the keyboard (Tab moves the focus on) Esc, then Tab; or Ctrl+M switches this on and off
Comment / uncomment Ctrl+/

With several cursors, everything you type, delete or paste happens at every cursor. Esc returns to one cursor.

The buttons ↩ (word wrap), · (show spaces and tabs), A− and A+ (font size) change the view; the editor remembers these settings.

Every document has its own undo history: ↶ and ↷ in the toolbar, or Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z.

Spelling: with a language chosen in the ABC selector of the header, unknown words are underlined – in plain text and Markdown everywhere, in program code only in comments and strings; right-click a word for suggestions ().

Split view

◫ shows the current document a second time, next to the first one (one above the other on phones), for example to look at the beginning of a long file while editing its end. Both views edit the same text and share one undo history; the second view follows the active tab. ◫ again closes it.

Find in files

🔍🗂 (Ctrl+Shift+F) searches all open documents at once: matches are listed by file with line and column; a click opens the document and selects the match. Aa matches upper/lower case exactly, .* treats the text as a regular expression. In Chrome and Edge, 📁 Folder… searches a folder on your computer instead, with its subfolders (skipping .git, node_modules, binary files and files over 5 MB); a click on a match opens that file. At most 2000 matches are listed.

Comparing

⇔ compares the current document with another open document or with a file. On wide screens the two texts are shown side by side – left the other text (read-only), right the current document – with changed lines and words highlighted and unchanged parts aligned (the changed lines are found line by line, like diff or git do, and in them the changed words – also in long texts with many changes); → between them copies a change of the left text into the document. On phones one view shows the deleted lines inline with Accept/Reject for each change. ↑/↓ jump between the differences; Done (or ⇔ again) ends the comparison, and edits made meanwhile become one undo step.

Tools

🛠 Tools in the toolbar changes the selected text, or the whole document when nothing is selected. Every tool can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

Group Tools
Lines sort A→Z or Z→A (numbers in natural order: 9 before 10; upper/lower case ignored), sort by length, reverse the order, remove duplicate lines, remove empty lines, trim whitespace at the end or at both ends, join lines
Case UPPER CASE, lower case, Title Case, iNVERT cASE
Encode / decode Base64 (UTF-8), URL encoding (percent encoding), HTML entities
Format format (indent) or minify JSON, format XML, format SQL, SQL on one line

Line tools always work on whole lines: those touched by the selection. Invalid input (for example broken JSON) shows a message and leaves the text unchanged.

Format SQL… works like the PoorSQL formatter: every clause on its own line, lists and sub-queries indented, keywords, function names and data types in UPPER CASE. A dialog sets the options, with a preview of the result: dialect (standard SQL, T-SQL/SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Oracle PL/SQL, Db2, DuckDB, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Spark, Hive, Trino), case of the keywords (upper, lower, as written), indentation (2 or 4 spaces, tab), layout (standard, or keywords in a column of their own, left- or right-aligned), AND/OR at the start or end of the line, the width up to which parentheses stay on one line, and the blank lines between statements. The options are remembered. SQL on one line removes comments (optimizer hints /*+ … */ stay) and line breaks; strings and quoted names stay unchanged.

Colours in the text

A small square in the colour stands in front of every hexadecimal colour (#6cf, #6cff, #66ccff, #66ccffff; in plain text and Markdown not in front of all-digit forms such as issue numbers #123). A click on it opens the colour picker of the suite: the colour in the text changes while you pick, OK makes it one step that Ctrl+Z undoes, Cancel restores it. The colour keeps its form – short or long, upper or lower case –, and an opacity part is added or removed as needed.

SAS programs

Files ending in .sas are highlighted as SAS: statements, procedure names, functions and CALL routines, macro statements (%let, %macro …), macro variables (&name.), formats (date9.), strings with their suffixes ('01jan2024'd), both kinds of comments (/* … */ and * … ;) and the lines of DATALINES/CARDS blocks. Lines inside DATA and PROC steps, DO blocks and macros are indented automatically; run;, quit;, end; and %mend; move back.

Code completion offers what fits where you type: procedure names after PROC, CALL routines after CALL, macro statements and functions after %, macro variables after & (those of %let, %global, %local, call symputx and macro parameters in the program, plus the automatic ones such as &sysdate9), and otherwise statements, functions and the names used in the program (data sets, variables). Suggestions follow the case you type (PROC PR → PRINT). Ctrl+Space opens the list at any time; Enter takes a suggestion, Esc closes the list.

Status bar

The status bar shows the cursor position (line and column), the length of the selection and the number of cursors. It also lets you change:

  • Language of the syntax highlighting (detected from the file name).
  • Encoding used when saving: UTF-8 (optionally with BOM), UTF-16 LE/BE or Windows-1252. When opening, the encoding is detected automatically. If a file was detected wrongly, Reload with encoding reads it again with another encoding (Chrome/Edge on the desktop).
  • Line endings used when saving: LF (Linux, macOS), CRLF (Windows) or CR.
  • Indentation: 2, 4 or 8 spaces, or tabs (shown 2, 4 or 8 characters wide). It is detected when a file is opened; the last choice is used for new documents. Tab indents with it; Ctrl+Alt+I always inserts a tab character.

Windows-1252 cannot store all characters. The editor warns before it replaces such characters with “?”.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.
